verses.t: This Jesus was the son of Sirach, and grand-childe to Jesus of the same name with him; This man therefore lived in the latter times, after the people had bene led away captive, and called home again, and almost after all the Prophets. Now his grandfather Jesus (as he himself witness) was a man of great diligence and wisdom among the Hebrewes, who did not onely gather the graue and short Sentences of wise men, that had bene before him, but himself also vttered some of his own, full of much vnderstanding and wisdom. When as therefore the first Jesus died, leauing this book almost perfected, Si rach his son receiuing it after him, left it to his own son Jesus, who hauing gotten it into his hands, compiled it all orderly into one Volume, and called it Wisdome, Intituling it, both by his own name, his fathers name, and his grandfathers, alluring the hearer by the very name of Wisdom, to have a greater love to the studie of this Book. It conteins therefore wise Sayings, darke Sentences, and Parables, and certaine particular ancient godly stories of men that pleased God. Also his Prayer and Song. Moreouer, what benefits God had vouchsafed his people, and what plagues he had heaped upon their enemies. This Jesus did imitate Solomon, and was no lesse famous for Wisdom, and learning, both being indeed a man of great learning, and so reputed also. Whereas many and great things have bene deliuered to us by the Law and the Prophets, and by others that have followed their steps, for the which things Israel ought to be commended for learning and Wisdom, and whereof not onely the Readers must needs become skilful themselues, but also they that desire to learne, be able to profit them which are without, both by speaking and writing : My grandfather Jesus, when he had much given himself to the reading of the Law, and the Prophets, and other Bookes of our fathers, and had gotten in it good judgment, was drawen on also himself, to write something pertayning to learning and Wisdom, to the intent that those which are desirous to learne, and are addicted to these things, might profit much more in living according to the Law. Therefore, let me intreat you to reade it with favor and attention, and to pardon Us, wherein we may secme to come short of some words which we have laboured to interprete. For the same things vttered in Hebrew, and translated into an other tongue, have not the same force in them : and not onely these things, but the Law it self, and the Prophets, and the rest of the Bookes, have no small difference, when they are spoken in their own language. For in the eight and thirtieth year comming into Egypt, when Euergetes was King, and continuing there some time, I found a Book of no small learning, therefore I thought it most necessary for me, to bestow some diligence and trauaile to interprete it: Vsing great watchfulnesse, and skill in that space, to bring the Book to an end, and set it foorth for them also, which in a strange countrey are willing to learne, being prepared before in maners to line after the Law. All wisdom comes from the Lord, and is with him for ever.
Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of raine, and the dayes of eternity?
Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deepe, and wisdom?
Wisdom has beene created before all things, and the vnderstanding of prudence from euerlasting.
The word of God most high, is the fountaine of wisdome, & her wayes are euerlasting commandements.
To whom has the root of wisdome beene reuealed? or who has knowen her wise counsels?
There is one wise and greatly to be feared; the Lord sitting upon his Throne.
He created her, and saw her, and numbred her, and powred her out upon all his works.
She with all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her to them that love him.
The feare of the Lord is honor, and glory, and gladnesse, and a crowne of reioycing.
The feare of the Lord makes a merrie heart, and gives ioy and gladnesse, and a long life.
Who so fears the Lord, it shall go well with him at the last, & he shall find favor in the day of his death.
To feare the Lord, is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithfull in the wombe.
She has built an euerlasting foundation with men, and she shal continue with their seede.
To feare the Lord, is fulnesse of wisdom, and fills men with her fruits.
She fills all their house with things desireable, and the garners with her increase.
The feare of the Lord is a crowne of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish, both which are the gifts of God: and it enlargs their reioycing that love him.
Wisdom rains downe skill and knowledge of vnderstanding, and exalts them to honor that holde her fast.
The root of wisdom is to feare the Lord, and the branches of it are long life.
The feare of the Lord drius away sins: and where it is present, it turns away wrath.
A furious man cannot be justified, for the sway of his fury shall be his destruction.
A patient man will beare for a time, and afterward ioy shall spring up to him.
He wil hide his words for a time, and the lippes of many shall declare his wisdom.
The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godlines is an abomination to a sinner.
If you desire wisdom, keepe the commaundements, and the Lord shall give her to you.
For the feare of the Lord is wisdome, and instruction: and faith and meekenesse are his delight.
Distrust not the feare of the Lord when you are poore: and come not to him with a double heart.
Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heede what you speak.

Exalt not yourself, lest you fall, and bring dishonor upon your soul, and so God discouer your secrets, and cast you downe in the midst of the congregation, because you came not in truth, to the feare of the Lord: but your heart is full of deceit.

verses.t: My son, if you come to serue the Lorde, prepare your soul for temptation.
Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.
Cleaue to him, and depart not away, that you may be increased at your last end.
Whatsoeuer is brought upon you, take cheerefully, and be patient when you are changed to a lowe estate.
For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of aduersitie.
Believe in him, and he will helpe you, order your way aright, and trust in him.
You that feare the Lord, waite for his mercy, and go not aside, lest you fall.
You that feare the Lord, believe him, and your reward shall not faile.
You that feare the Lord, hope for good, and for euerlasting ioy and mercy.
Looke at the generations of old, and see, did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his feare, & was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?
For the Lord is full of compassion, and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitifull, and forgius sins, and saus in time of affliction.
Woe be to fearefull hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goes two wayes.
Woe to him that is faint hearted, for he beleeus not, therefore shall he not be defended.
Woe to you that have lost patience: and what will you do when the Lord shall visite you?
They that feare the Lord, will not disobey his word, and they that love him, will keepe his wayes.
They that feare the Lord, will seeke that which is well pleasing to him, and they that love him, shall be filled with the Law.
They that feare the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight:
Saying, We will fal into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men: for as his maiestie is, so is his mercy.

verses.t: Heare me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.
For the Lord has given the father honor over the children, and has confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.
Who so honours his father, makes an atonement for his sins.
And he that honours his mother, is as one that layes up treasure.
Who so honours his father, shal have ioy of his own children, and when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
He that honours his father, shal have a long life, and he that is obedient to the Lord, shall be a comfort to his mother.
He that fears the Lord, will honor his father, and will do seruice to his parents, as to his masters.
Honor your father and mother, both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.
For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children, but the curse of the mother roots out foundations.
Glory not in the dishonour of your father, for your fathers dishonour is no glory to you.
For the glory of a man, is from the honor of his father, and a mother in dishonour, is a reproch to the children.
My son, helpe your father in his age, and grieue him not as long as he lius.
And if his vnderstanding faile, have patience with him, and despise him not, when you are in your ful strength.
For the relieuing of your father shall not be forgotten: and in stead of sins it shall be added to build you up.
In the day of your affliction it shall be remembred, your sins also shal melt away, as the yce in þ faire warme weather.
He that forsaks his father, is as a blasphemer, and he that angrs his mother, is cursed of God.
My son, go on with your businesse in meekenesse, so shall you be beloued of him that is approued.
The greater you are, the more humble yourself, and you shall find favor before the Lord.
Many are in high place and of renowne: but mysteries are reueiled to the meeke.
For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.
Seeke not out the things that are too hard for you, neither search the things that are aboue your strength.
But what is commaunded you, think thereupon with reuerence, for it is not needfull for you, to see with your eyes, the things that are in secret.
Be not curious in vnnecessarie matters: for moe things are showed to you, then men vnderstand.
For many are deceiued by their own vaine opinion, and an evil suspition has ouerthrowen their judgment.
Without eyes you shall want light: professe not the knowledge therfore that you have not.
A stubborne heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loves danger shall perish in it.
An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrowes, and the wicked man shall heape sin upon sin.
In the punishment of the proud there is no remedie: for the plant of wickedness has taken roote in him.
The heart of the prudent will vnderstand a parable, and an attentiue eare is the desire of a wise man.
Water will quench a flaming fire, and alms makes an attonement for sins.
And he that requits good turnes, is mindfull of that which may come heereafter: and when he falls he shall find a stay.

verses.t: My son, defraude not the poore of his living, and make not the needy eies to waite long.
Make not an hungry soul sorrowfull, neither prouoke a man in his distresse.
Adde not more trouble to an heart that is vexed, and deferre not to give to him that is in neede.
Reiect not the supplication of the afflicted, neither turne away your face from a poore man.
Turne not away your eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse you:
For if he curse you in the bitternesse of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.
Get yourself the love of the congregation, and bow your head to a great man.
Let it not grieue you to bowe downe your eare to the poore, and give him a friendly answere with meekenesse.
Deliuer him that suffrs wrong, from the hand of the oppressour, and be not faint hearted when you sit in judgment.
Be as a father to the fatherlesse, and in stead of a husband to their mother, so shall you be as the son of the most high, and he shall love you more then your mother does.
Wisdom exalts her children, and layes hold of them that seeke her.
He that loves her, loves life, and they that seeke to her earely, shall be filled with ioy.
He that holds her fast shall inherit glory, and wheresoeuer she entrs, the Lord will blesse.
They that serue her shall minister to the Holy one, and them that love her, the Lord does love.
Who so gives eare to her, shall judge the nations, and he that attends to her, shall dwell securely.
If a man commit himself to her, he shall inherite her, and his generation shall hold her in possession.
For at the first she will walke with him by crooked wayes, and bring feare and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her Lawes.
Then wil she returne the straight way to him, and comfort him, and show him her secrets.
But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruine.
Obserue the opportunitie, and beware of evil, and be not ashamed when it concerns your soul.
For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame which is glory and grace.
Accept no person against your soul, and let not the reuerence of any man cause you to fall:
And refraine not to speake, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not your wisdom in her beautie.
For by speach wisdom shall be knowen, and learning by the word of the tongue.
In no wise speake against the truth, but be abashed of the errour of your ignorance.
Be not ashamed to confesse your sins, and force not the course of the riuer.
Make not yourself an vnderling to a foolish man, neither accept the person of the mighty.
Striue for the truth to death, and the Lord shall fight for you.
Be not hastie in your tongue, and in your deeds slacke and remisse.
Be not as a Lion in your house, nor franticke among your seruants.
Let not your hand be stretched out to receiue, and shut when you should repay.

verses.t: Set not your heart upon your goods, and say not, I have ynough for my life.
Folow not your own minde, and your strength, to walke in the wayes of your heart:
And say not, Who shall controll me for my works? for the Lord will surely reuenge your pride.
Say not, I have sinned, and what harme has happened to me? for the Lord is long suffering, he wil in no wise let you go.
Concerning propitiation, be not without feare to adde sin to sin.
And say not, His mercy is great, he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation rests upon sinners.

Make no tarying to turne to the Lord, and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shal the wrath of the Lord come foorth, and in your securitie you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
Set not your heart upon goods vniustly gotten: for they shall not profit you in the day of calamitie.
Winnow not with every winde, and go not into every way: for so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
Be stedfast in your vnderstanding, and let your word be the same.
Be swift to heare, and let your life be sincere, & with patience give answere.
If you have vnderstanding, answer your neighbor, if not, lay your hand upon your mouth.
Honor and shame is in talke; and the tongue of man is his fall.
Be not called a whisperer, and lye not in wait with your tongue: for a foule shame is upon the thiefe, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue.
Be not ignorant of any thing, in a great matter or a small.

verses.t: Do no evil, so shall no harme come to you.
Depart from the vniust, and iniquitie shall turne away from you.
My son, sow not upon the furrowes of vnrighteousnesse, and you shall not reape them seuen folde.
Seeke not of the Lord preheminence, neither of the King the seate of honor.
Iustifie not yourself before the Lord, and boast not of your wisdom before the king.
Seeke not to be judge, being not able to take away iniquitie, lest at any time you feare the person of the mightie, and lay a stumbling blocke in the way of your vprightnesse.
Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then you shall not cast yourself downe among the people.
Bind not one sin upon another, for in one you shall not be vnpunished.
Say not, God wil looke upon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most High God, he will accept it.
Be not faint hearted when you make your prayer, and neglect not to give alms.
Laugh no man to scorne in the bitternesse of his soul: for there is one which humbls and exalts.
Deuise not a lie against your brother: neither do the like to your friend.
Use not to make any maner of lie: for the custome of it is not good.
Use not many words in a multitude of Elders, and make not much babling when you pray.
Hate not laborious work, neither husbandrie, which the most High has ordeined.
Number not yourself among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tary long.
Humble your soul greatly: for the vengeance of the vngodly is fire and wormes.
Change not a friend for any good by no meanes: neither a faithfull brother for the gold of Ophir.
Forgoe not a wise and good woman: for her grace is aboue gold.
Whereas your seruant works truely, entreate him not evil, nor the hireling that bestows himself wholly for you.
Let your soul love a good seruant, and defraud him not of liberty.
Have you cattell? have an eye to them, and if they be for your profit, keepe them with you.
Have you children? instruct them, and bow downe their necke from their youth.
Have you daughters? have care of their body, and shewe not yourself cheerefull toward them.
Marrie your daughter, and so shall you have performed a weightie matter: but give her to a man of vnderstanding.
Have you a wife after your minde? forsake her not, but give not yourself over to a light woman.
Honor your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrowes of your mother.
Remember that you were begot of them, and how can you recompense them the things that they have done for you?
Feare the Lord with all your soul, and reuerence his priests.
Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.

Feare the Lord, and honor the priest: and give him his portion, as it is commanded you, the first fruits, and the trespasse offering, & the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things.
And stretch your hand to the poore, that your blessing may be perfected
A gift has grace in the sight of every man living, and for the dead deteine it not.
Faile not to be with them that weepe, and mourne with them that mourne.
Be not slow to visit the sicke: for that shall make you to be beloued.
Whatsoeuer you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amisse.

verses.t: Striue not with a mighty man, lest you fall into his hands.
Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he ouerweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and peruerted the hearts of kings.
Striue not with a man that is full of tongue, and heape not wood upon his fire.
Iest not with a rude man, lest your ancestours be disgraced.
Reproch not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
Dishonour not a man in his old age: for euen some of us waxe old.
Reioice not over your greatest enemie being dead, but remember that we die all.
Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint yourself with their prouerbs; for of them you shall learne instruction, & how to serue great men with ease.
Misse not the discourse of the Elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learne vnderstanding, and to give answere as need requires.
Kindle not the coales of a sinner, lest you be burnt with the flame of his fire.
Rise not up (in anger) at the presence of an iniurious person, least he lie in waite to entrap you in your words.
Lend not to him that is mightier then yourself; for if you lend him, count it but lost.
Be not surety aboue your power: for if you be surety, take care to pay it.
Go not to law with a judge, for they will judge for him according to his honor.
Trauaile not by the way with a bold fellow, least he become grieuous to you: for he will do according to his own will, and you shall perish with him through his folly.
Striue not with an angry man, and go not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no helpe, he will ouerthrow you.
Consult not with a foole; for he cannot keepe counsell.
Do no secret thing before a stranger, for you know not what he will bring forth.
Open not your heart to every man, least he requite you with a shrewd turne.

verses.t: Be not iealous over the wife of your bosome, and teach her not an evil lesson against yourself.
Give not your soul to a woman, to set her foot upon your substance.
Meete not with an harlot, least you fall into her snares.
Use not much the companie of a woman that is a singer, least you be taken with her attempts.
Gaze not on a maide, that you fall not by those things, that are pretious in her.
Give not your soul to harlots, that you loose not your inheritance.
Looke not round about you, in the streets of the city, neither wander you in the solitary places of it.
Turne away your eye from a beautifull woman, and looke not upon anothers beautie: for many have beene deceiued by the beautie of a woman, for heerewith love is kindled as a fire.

Sit not at all with another mans wife, nor sit downe with her in your armes, and spend not your money with her at the wine, least your heart incline to her, and so thorough your desire you fall into destruction.
Forsake not an old friend, for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine: when it is old, you shall drinke it with pleasure.
Enuy not the glory of a sinner: for you know not what shall be his end.
Delight not in the thing that the vngodly have pleasure in, but remember they shall not go vnpunished to their graue.

Keepe you farre from the man that has power to kill, so shall you not doubt the feare of death: and if you come to him, make no fault, least he take away your life presently: remember that you go in the midst of snares, and that you walk upon the battlements of the city.
As near as you can, ghesse at your neighbor, and consult with the wise.
Let your talke be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the most high.
And let just men eat and drinke with you, and let your glorying be in the feare of the Lord.
For the hand of the artificer, the work shall be commended: and the wise ruler of the people, for his speech.
A man of an ill tongue is dangerous in his city, and he that is rash in his talke shall be hated.

In the hand of God is the prosperitie of man: and upon the person of the scribe shall he lay his honor.

Pride is hatefull before God, and man: and by both does one commit iniquitie.
Because of unrighteous dealings, iniuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdom is translated from one people to another.
Why is earth and ashes proude? There is not a more wicked thing, then a couetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale, because while he lius, he casts away his bowels.
The Phisition cuts off a long disease, and he that is to day a King, to morrow shall die.
For when a man is dead, he shall inherite creeping things, beastes and wormes.

For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it, shall powre out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and ouerthrew them vtterly.
The Lord has cast downe the thrones of proud Princes, and set up the meeke in their stead.
The Lord has plucked up the rootes of the proud nations: and planted the lowly in their place.
The Lord ouerthrew countreys of the heathen: and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
He tooke some of them away, and destroyed them, and has made their memoriall to cease from the earth.
Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are borne of a woman.

They that feare the Lord are a sure seed, and they that love him, an honourable plant: they that regard not the Law, are a dishonourable seed, they that transgresse the commandements, are a deceiuable seed.

Whether he be rich, noble, or poore, their glory is the feare of the Lord.

Better is he that labours and abounds in all things, then he that boasts himself, and wants bread.
My son, glorifie your soul in meekenesse, and give it honor according to the dignitie of it.

The poore man is honoured for his skill, and the rich man is honoured for his riches.
He that is honoured in pouertie, how much more in riches? And he that is dishonourable in riches, how much more in pouertie?

verses.t: Wisdom lifts up the head of him that is of low degree, and makes him to sit among great men.
Commend not a man for his beautie, neither abhorre a man for his outward appearance.
The Be is little among such as flie, but her fruite is the chiefe of sweete things.
Boast not of your cloathing and clothing, and exalt not yourself in the day of honor: for the works of the Lord are wonderfull, and his works among men are hidden.
Many kings have sit downe upon the ground, and one that was never thought of, has worne the crowne.
Many mightie men have beene greatly disgraced: and the honourable deliuered into other mens hands.
Blame not before you have examined the truth: vnderstand first, and then rebuke.
Answere not, before you have heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talke.
Striue not in a matter that concerns you not: and sit not in judgment with sinners.
My son, meddle not with many matters: for if you meddle much, you shall not be innocent: and if you follow after, you shall not obtaine, neither shall you escape by flying.
There is one that labours and takes paines, and makes haste, and is so much the more behinde.
Again, there is another that is slow, and has neede of helpe, wanting abilitie, and full of pouertie, yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,
And lifted up his head from miserie, so that many that saw it, marueiled at him.

Many kings have sit downe upon the ground, and one that was never thought of, has worne the crowne.

verses.t: When you will do good, know to whō you do it, so shall you be thanked for your benefites.
Do good to the godly man, and you shall find a recompence, and if not from him, yet from the most high.
There can no good come to him that is always occupied in evil: nor to him that gives no alms.
Give to the godly man, and helpe not a sinner.

Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the vngodly: hold backe your bread, and give it not to him, lest he ouermaster you thereby. For you shall receiue twice as much evil, for all the good you shall have done to him.
For the most High hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the vngodly, and keeps them against the mightie day of their punishment.
Give to the good, and helpe not the sinner.
A friend cannot be knowen in prosperitie, and an enemy cannot be hidden in aduersitie.
In the prosperitie of a man, enemies will be grieued, but in his aduersitie, euen a friend will depart.
Never trust your enemie: for like as yron rusts, so is his wickedness.

Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed, and beware of him, and you shall be to him, as if you had wiped a looking glasse, and you shall knowe that his rust has not beene altogether wiped away.

Set him not by you, lest when he has ouerthrowen you, he stand up in your place, neither let him sit at your right hand, lest he seeke to take your seat, and you at the last remember my words, and be pricked with it.
Who will pitie a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, or any such as come near wilde beasts?
So one that goes to a sinner, and is defiled with him in his sins, who will pitie?
For a while he will abide with you, but if you begin to fall, he wil not tarie.
An enemie speaks sweetly with his lippes, but in his heart he imagins how to throw you into a pit: he will weepe with his eyes, but if he find opportunitie, he will not be satisfied with blood.
If aduersitie come upon you, you shall find him there first, & though he pretend to helpe you, yet shal he vndermine you.
He will shake his head and clap his handes, and whisper much, and change his countenance.

verses.t: He that touches pitch, shal be defiled with it, and he that has fellowship with a proude man, shall be like to him.

Burthen not yourself aboue your power, while you liu, and have no fellowship with one that is mightier, and richer then yourself. For how agree the kettle and the earthen pot together? for if the one be smitten against the other, it shall be broken.
The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threatns withall: the poore is wronged, and he must intreat also.
If you be for his profit, he will vse you: but if you have nothing, he will forsake you.
If you have any thing, he will live with you, indeed he will make you bare, and will not be sorie for it.
If he have need of you, he will deceiue you, and smile upon you, and put you in hope, he will speake you faire, and say, What want you?

And he will shame you by his meates, until he have drawen you drie twice or thrice, and at the last he will laugh you to scorne: afterward when he sees you, he will forsake you, and shake his head at you.
Beware that you be not deceiued, and brought downe in your iolitie.
If you be inuited of a mighty man, withdraw yourself, and so much the more will he inuite you.
Presse you not upon him, lest you be put backe, stand not farre off, lest you be forgotten.
Affect not to be made equall to him in talke, and believe not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt you, and smiling upon you will get out your secrets.
But cruelly he will lay up your words, and will not spare to do you hurt, and to put you in prison.
Obserue and take good heed, for you walk in peril of your ouerthrowing: when you hear these things, awake in your sleepe.
Love the Lord all your life, and call upon him for your saluation.
Every beast loves his like, and every man loves his neighbor.
All flesh consorts according to kind, and a man will cleaue to his like:
What fellowship has the wolfe with the lambe? so the sinner with the godly.
What agreement is there betweene the Hyena and a dogge? and what peace betweene the rich and the poore?
As the wilde asse is the lyons pray in the wildernesse: so the rich eat up the poore.
As the proud hate humilitie: so does the rich abhorre the poore.
A rich man beginning to fall, is held up of his friends: but a poore man being downe, is thrust also away by his friends.

When a rich man is fallen, he has many helpers: he speaks things not to be spoken, and yet men iustifie him: the poore man slipt, and yet they rebuked him too: he spoke wisely, and could have no place.

When a rich man speaks, every man holds his tongue, and looke what he sayes, they extoll it to the clouds: but if the poore man speake, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will helpe to ouerthrowe him.
Riches are good to him that has no sin, and pouerty is evil in the mouth of the vngodly.
The heart of a man changs his countenance, whether it be for good or evil: and a merry heart makes a cheerefull countenance.
A cheerefull countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity, and the finding out of parables, is a wearisome labour of the minde.

verses.t: Blessed is the man that has not slipt with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins.
Blessed is he whose conscience has not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in the Lord.
Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an enuious man do with money?
He that gathers by defrauding his own soul, gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? he shall not take pleasure in his goods.
There is none worse then he that enuies himself; and this is a recompence of his wickedness.
And if he does good, he does it vnwillingly, and at the last he will declare his wickedness.
The enuious man has a wicked eye, he turns away his face and despises men.
A couetous mans eye is not satisfied with his portion, and the iniquity of the wicked dries up his soul.
A wicked eye enuies bread, and he is a niggard at his table.
My son, according to your habilitie do good to yourself, and give the Lord his due offering.
Remember that death will not be long in comming, and that the couenant of the graue is not showed to you.
Do good to your friend before you die, and according to your abilitie, stretch out your hand and give to him.
Defraud not yourself of the good day, and let not the part of a good desire ouerpasse you.
Shall you not leaue your trauailes to another? and your labours to be diuided by lot?
Give, and take, and sanctifie your soul, for there is no seeking of dainties in the graue.
All flesh waxes old as a garment: for the couenant from the beginning is; you shall die the death.
As of the greene leaues on a thicke tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one comes to an end, and another is borne.
Every work rots and consums away, and the worker therof shal go withall.
Blessed is the man that does meditate good things in wisdome, and that reasons of holy things by his vnderstanding.
He that considers her wayes in his heart, shall also have vnderstanding in her secrets.
Go after her as one that tracs, and lie in wait in her wayes.
He that pries in at her windowes, shal also hearken at her doores.
He that does lodge near her house, shall also fasten a pin in her walles.
He shall pitch his tent near to her, and shall lodge in a lodging where good things are.
He shal set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches.
By her he shall be couered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.

verses.t: He that fears the Lord will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the Law shal obtaine her.
And as a mother shall she meet him, and receiue him as a wife maried of a virgin.
With the bread of vnderstanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisdom to drinke.
He shall be stayed upon her, and shall not be moued, and shall rely upon her, and shall not be confounded.
She shall exalt him aboue his neighbours, and in the midst of the congregation shall she open his mouth.
He shall find ioy, and a crowne of gladnesse, and she shall cause him to inherit an euerlasting name.
But foolish men shall not attaine to her, and sinners shall not see her.
For she is farre from pride, and men that are liers cannot remember her.
Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of the Lord:
For praise shall be vttered in wisdome, and the Lord wil prosper it.
Say not you, It is through the Lord, that I fell away, for you ought not to do the things that he hates.
Say not you, He has caused me to erre, for he has no need of the sinfull man.
The Lord hates all abomination, and they that feare God love it not.
He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsell,
If you will, to keepe the Commandements, and to performe acceptable faithfulnesse.
He has set fire and water before you: stretch forth your hand to whether you will.
Before man is life and death, and whether him likes shall be given him.
For the wisdom of the Lord is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things,
And his eyes are upon them that feare him, & he knows every work of man.
He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man license to sin.

verses.t: Desire not a multitude of vnprofitable children, neither delight in vngodly sons.
Though they multiply, reioyce not in them, except the feare of the Lord be with them.
Trust not you in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just, is better then a thousand, and better it is to die without children, then to have them that are vngodly.
For by one that has vnderstanding, shall the city be replenished, but the kindred of the wicked, shall speedily become desolate.
Many such things have I seene with my eyes, and my eare has heard greater things then these.
In the congregation of the vngodly, shall a fire be kindled, and in a rebellious nation, wrath is set on fire.
He was not pacified towards the olde giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishnesse.
Neither spared he the place where Lot soiourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
He pitied not the people of perdition, who were taken away in their sins.
Nor the sixe hundredth thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardnesse of their hearts.
And if there be one stiffe-necked among the people, it is marueile, if he escape vnpunished; for mercy and wrath are with him, he is mighty to forgive, and to powre out displeasure.
As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he iudgs a man according to his works.
The sinner shall not escape with his spoiles, and the patience of the godly shall not be frustrate.
Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerfull works might be knowen to the world.
His mercy is manifest to every creature, and he has separated his light from the darkness with an Adamant.
Say not you, I will hide myself from the Lord: shall any remember me from aboue? I shall not be remembred among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
Look, the heaven, and the heaven of heauens, the deepe and the earth, and all that in it is, shall be mooued when he shall visit.
The mountaines also, and foundations of the earth shall be shaken with trembling, when the Lord looks upon them.
No heart can think upon these things worthily: and who is able to conceiue his wayes?
It is a tempest, which no man can see: for the most part of his works are hidde.
Who can declare the works of his justice? or who can endure them? for his Couenant is afarre off, and the triall of all things is in the ende.
He that wants vnderstanding, will think upon vaine things: and a foolish man erring, imagins follies.
My son, hearken to me, and learne knowledge, and marke my words with your heart.
I will shewe foorth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly.
The works of the Lord are done in judgment from the beginning: and from the time he made them, he disposed the parts of it.
He garnished his works for ever, and in his hand are the chiefe of them to all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their works.
None of them hindrs another, and they shall never disobey his word.
After this, the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with his blessings.
With all maner of living things has he couered the face of it, and they shall returne into it again.

His mercy is manifest to every creature, and he has separated his light from the darkness with an Adamant. Say not you, I will hide myself from the Lord: shall any remember me from aboue? I shall not be remembred among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?

Look, the heaven, and the heaven of heauens, the deepe and the earth, and all that in it is, shall be mooued when he shall visit. The mountaines also, and foundations of the earth shall be shaken with trembling, when the Lord looks upon them. No heart can think upon these things worthily: and who is able to conceiue his wayes? It is a tempest, which no man can see: for the most part of his works are hidde. Who can declare the works of his justice? or who can endure them? for his Couenant is afarre off, and the triall of all things is in the ende.

He that wants vnderstanding, will think upon vaine things: and a foolish man erring, imagins follies. My son, hearken to me, and learne knowledge, and marke my words with your heart. I will shewe foorth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly. The works of the Lord are done in judgment from the beginning: and from the time he made them, he disposed the parts of it. He garnished his works for ever, and in his hand are the chiefe of them to all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their works.

None of them hindrs another, and they shall never disobey his word. After this, the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with his blessings. With all maner of living things has he couered the face of it, and they shall returne into it again.

verses.t: The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.
He gaue them few dayes, and a short time, and power also over the things in it.
He endued them with strength by themselues, and made them according to his image,
And put the feare of man upon all flesh, and gaue him dominion over beasts and foules.
Counsell, and a tongue, and eyes, eares, and a heart, gaue he them to vnderstand.
Withall, he filled them with the knowledge of vnderstanding, & showed them good and evil.
He set his eye upon their hearts, that he might show them the greatnesse of his works.
He gaue them to glory in his marueilous actes for ever, that they might declare his works with vnderstanding.
And the elect shall praise his holy Name.
Beside this he gaue them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
He made an euerlasting couenant with them, and showed them his iudgements.
Their eyes saw the maiestie of his glory, and their eares heard his glorious voice.
And he said to them, Beware of all vnrighteousnes, and he gaue every man commandement concerning his neighbor,
Their wayes are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
Every man from his youth is given to evil, neither could they make to themselues fleshie hearts for stonie.
For in the diuision of the nations of the whole earth, he set a ruler over every people, but Israel is the Lords portion.
Whom being his first borne, he nourishes with discipline, and giuing him the light of his love, does not forsake him.
Therefore all their works are as the Sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their wayes.
None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before the Lord:
But the Lord being gracious, and knowing his workemanship, neither left nor forsooke them, but spared them.
The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man, as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters.
Afterward he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompense upon their heads.
But to them that repent, he granted them returne, and comforted those that faile in patience.
Returne to the Lord, and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend lesse.
Turne again to the most High, and turne away from iniquitie: for he will leade you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.
Who shall praise the most High in the graue, in stead of them which live and give thanks?
Thankesgiuing perishes from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart, shall praise the Lord.
How great is the louing kindnes of the Lord our God, and his compassion to such as turne to him in holinesse?
For all things cannot be in men, because þ son of man is not immortal.
What is brighter then the Sun? yet the light of it fails: and flesh and blood will imagine evil.
He views the power of the height of heaven, and all men are but earth and ashes.

verses.t: He that lius for ever, created all things in generall.
The Lord onely is righteous, and there is none other but he.
Who gouerns the world with the palme of his hand, and all things obey his will, for he is the king of all, by his power diuiding holy things among them from prophane.
To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble actes?
Who shall number the strength of his maiestie? and who shall also tel out his mercies?
As for the wonderous works of the Lord, there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out.
When a man has done, then he begins, and when he leaus off, then he shall be doubtfull.
What is man, and whereto serus he? what is his good, & what is his evil?
The number of a mans dayes at the most are an hundred years.
As a drop of water to the Sea, and a grauell stone in comparison of the sand, so are a thousand years to the dayes of eternitie.
Therfore is God patient with them, & powrs forth his mercy upon them.
He saw and perceiued their end to be evil, therefore he multiplied his compassion.
The mercy of man is toward his neighbor, but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh: he reproous and nurturs, and teaches, & brings again as a shepherd his flocke.
He has mercy on them that receiue discipline, and that diligently seeke after his iudgements.
My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither vse vncomfortable words when you give any thing.
Shall not the deaw asswage the heate? so is a word better then a gift.
Loe is not a word better then a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
A foole will vpbraide churlishly, and a gift of the enuious consums the eyes.
Learne before you speake, and vse phisicke, or ever you be sicke.
Before judgment examine yourself, and in the day of visitation you shall find mercy.
Humble yourself before you be sicke, and in the time of sins show repentance.
Let nothing hinder you to pay your vowe in due time, and deferre not until death to be justified.
Before you pray, prepare yourself, and be not as one that tempts the Lord.
Think upon the wrath that shall be at the end; and the time of vengeance when he shall turne away his face.
When you have enough remember the time of hunger, and when you are rich think upon pouerty and need.
From the morning until the evening the time is changed, and all things are soone done before the Lord.
A wise man will feare in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a foole will not obserue time.
Every man of vnderstanding knows wisdom, and wil give praise to him that found her.
They that were of vnderstanding in sayings, became also wise themselues, and powred forth exquisite parables.
Go not after your lustes, but refraine yourself from your appetites.
If you give your soul the desires that please her, she will make you a laughing stocke to your enemies, that maligne you.
Take not pleasure in much good cheere, neither be tyed to the expence of it.
Be not made a begger by banquetting upon borrowing, when you have nothing in your purse, for you shall lie in waite for your own life: and be talked on.

verses.t: A labouring man that is given to drunkennesse shal not be rich, and he that contemns small things shall fall by little & little.
Wine and women will make men of vnderstanding to fall away, and he that cleaus to harlots will become impudent.
Mothes and wormes shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.
He that is hasty to give credit is light minded, and he that sins shall offend against his own soul.
Who so takes pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned, but he that resists pleasures, crowns his life.
He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife, and he that hates babbling, shall have lesse evil.
Rehearse not to another that which is told to you, and you shall fare never the worse.
Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other mens liues, and if you can without offence reueale them not.
For he heard and obserued you, and when time comes he will hate you.
If you have heard a word, let it die with you, and be bold it will not burst you.
A foole trauails with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.
As an arrowe that sticks in a mans thigh, so is a word within a fooles belly.
Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it, and if he have that he do it no more.
Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it, and if he have, that he speake it not again.
Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, & believe not every tale.
There is one that slips in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that has not offended with his tongue?
Admonish your neighbor before you threaten him, and not being angry give place to the Law of the most high.
The feare of the Lord is the first step to be accepted and wisdom obtains his love.
The knowledge of the Commandements of the Lord, is the doctrine of life, and they that do things that please him, shall receiue the fruit of the tree of immortalitie.
The feare of the Lord is all wisdom, and in all wisdom is the performance of the Law, and the knowledge of his omnipotencie.
If a seruant say to his master, I will not do as it pleases you, though afterward he do it, he angers him that nourishes him.
The knowledge of wickednes is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsell of sinners, prudence.
There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination, and there is a foole wanting in wisdom.
He that has smal vnderstanding and fears God, is better then one that has much wisdom, and transgress the Law of the most High.
There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is vniust, and there is one that turns aside to make judgment appeare: and there is a wise man that iustifies in judgment.
There is a wicked man that hangs downe his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
Casting downe his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not knowen, he will do you a mischiefe before you be aware.
And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he finds opportunitie he wil do evil.
A man may be knowen by his looke, and one that has vnderstanding, by his countenance, when you meet him.
A mans attire, and excessiue laughter, and gate, show what he is.

verses.t: There is a reproofe that is not comely: again some man holds his tongue, and he is wise.
It is much better to reprooue, then to be angry secretly, and he that confesses his fault, shall be preserued from hurt.
How good is it when you are reproued, to show repentance? for so shall you escape wilfull sin.
As is the lust of an Eunuch to defloure a virgine; so is he that executs judgment with violence.
There is one that keeps silence and is found wise: and another by much babling becoms hatefull.
Some man holds his tongue, because he has not to answere, and some keeps silence, knowing his time.
A wise man wil hold his tongue till he see opportunitie: but a babler and a foole will regard no time.
He that vses many words shall be abhorred; and he that takes to himself authority in it, shall be hated.
There is a sinner that has good successe in evil things; and there is a gaine that turns to losse.
There is a gift that shall not profit you; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.
There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifts up his head from a low estate.
There is that buyes much for a little, and repays it seuen fold.
A wise man by his words makes himself beloued: but the graces of fooles shall be powred out.
The gift of a foole shall do you no good when you have it; neither yet of the enuious for his necessitie: for he looks to receiue many things for one.
He gives little and vpbraids much; he opens his mouth like a crier; to day he lends, and to morrow will he aske it again: such an one is to be hated of God and man.
The foole says, I have no friends, I have no thanke for all my good deeds: and they that eat my bread speake evil of me.
How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorne? for he knows not aright what it is to have; and it is all one to him, as if he had it not.
To slip upon a pauement, is better then to slip with the tongue: so, the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
An vnseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the vnwise.
A wise sentence shall be reiected when it comes out of a fools mouth: for he will not speake it in due season.
There is that is hindred from sinning through want: and when he takes rest, he shall not be troubled.
There is that destroys his own soul through bashfulnesse, and by accepting of persons ouerthrows himself.
There is that for bashfulnes promises to his friend, and makes him his enemy for nothing.
A lie is a foule blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the vntaught.
A thiefe is better then a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.
The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.
A wise man shall promote himself to honor with his words: and he that has vnderstanding, will please great men.
He that tils his land, shall increase his heape: and he that pleases great men, shal get pardon for iniquity.
Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stoppe up his mouth that he cannot reprooue.
Wisdom that is hidde, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
Better is he that hides his folly, then a man that hides his wisdom.
Necessary patience in seeking the Lord, is better then he that leads his life without a guide.

verses.t: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but aske pardon for your former sins.
Flee from sin as from the face of a Serpent: for if you com too near it, it will bite you: the teeth of it, are as the teeth of a lyon, slaying the souls of men.
All iniquitie is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.
To terrifie and do wrong, will waste riches: thus the house of proude men shall be made desolate.
A prayer out of a poore mans mouth reaches to the eares of God, and his judgment comes speedily.
He that hates to be reprooued, is in the way of sinners: but he that fears the Lord, will repent from his heart.
An eloquent man is knowen farre and near, but a man of vnderstanding knows when he slips.
He that builds his house with other mens money, is like one that gathers himself stones for the tombe of his buriall.
The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.
The way of sinners is made plaine with stones, but at the ende of it is the pit of hell.
He that keeps the Law of the Lord, gets the vnderstanding of it: and the perfection of the feare of the Lord, is wisdom.
He that is not wise, will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplies bitternesse.
The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsell is like a pure fountaine of life.
The inner parts of a foole, are like a broken vessell, and he will holde no knowledge as long as he lius.
If a skilfull man heare a wise word, he will commend it, and adde to it: but assoone as one of no vnderstanding hears it, it displeases him, and he casts it behinde his backe.
The talking of a foole is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
They inquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a foole: and the knowledge of the vnwise, is as talke without sense.
Doctrine to fooles, is as fetters on the feete, and like manacles on the right hand.
A foole lifts up his voice with laughter, but a wise man does scarce smile a litle.
Learning is to a wise man, as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arme.
A foolish mans foote is soone in his house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.
A foole will peepe in at the doore into the house, but he that is well nurtured, will stand without.
It is the rudenesse of a man to hearken at the doore: but a wise man will be grieued with the disgrace.
The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertaine not to them: but the words of such as have vnderstanding, are weighed in the ballance.
The heart of fooles is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
When the vngodly curses Satan, he curses his own soul.
A whisperer defils his own soul, and is hated wheresoeuer he dwells.

A prayer out of a poore mans mouth reaches to the eares of God, and his judgment comes speedily.

He that hates to be reprooued, is in the way of sinners: but he that fears the Lord, will repent from his heart. An eloquent man is knowen farre and near, but a man of vnderstanding knows when he slips. He that builds his house with other mens money, is like one that gathers himself stones for the tombe of his buriall. The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.

The way of sinners is made plaine with stones, but at the ende of it is the pit of hell. He that keeps the Law of the Lord, gets the vnderstanding of it: and the perfection of the feare of the Lord, is wisdom. He that is not wise, will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplies bitternesse. The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsell is like a pure fountaine of life. The inner parts of a foole, are like a broken vessell, and he will holde no knowledge as long as he lius.

If a skilfull man heare a wise word, he will commend it, and adde to it: but assoone as one of no vnderstanding hears it, it displeases him, and he casts it behinde his backe. The talking of a foole is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise. They inquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart. As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a foole: and the knowledge of the vnwise, is as talke without sense.

Doctrine to fooles, is as fetters on the feete, and like manacles on the right hand. A foole lifts up his voice with laughter, but a wise man does scarce smile a litle. Learning is to a wise man, as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arme. A foolish mans foote is soone in his house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him. A foole will peepe in at the doore into the house, but he that is well nurtured, will stand without.

It is the rudenesse of a man to hearken at the doore: but a wise man will be grieued with the disgrace. The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertaine not to them: but the words of such as have vnderstanding, are weighed in the ballance. The heart of fooles is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
When the vngodly curses Satan, he curses his own soul. A whisperer defils his own soul, and is hated wheresoeuer he dwells.

verses.t: A slouthful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hisse him out to his disgrace.
A slouthfull man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up, will shake his hand.
An evil nurtured son is the dishonour of his father that begate him: and a daughter is borne to his losse.
A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that lius dishonestly, is her fathers heauinesse.
She that is bold, dishonours both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her.
A tale out of season musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisdom are never out of time.
Who so teaches a foole, is as one that glews a potsheard together, and as he that wakes one from a sound sleepe.
He that tells a tale to a foole, speaks to one in a slumber: when he has told his tale, he will say, What is the matter?
If children live honestly, and have wherwithall, they shall couer the basenesse of their parents.
But children being haughtie through disdaine, and want of nurture, do staine the nobilitie of their kinred.
Weepe for the dead, for he has lost the light: and weepe for the foole, for he wants vnderstanding: make litle weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the foole is worse then death.
Seuen dayes do men mourne for him that is dead; but for a foole, and an vngodly man, all the dayes of his life.

Talke not much with a foole, and go not to him that has no vnderstanding, beware of him lest you have trouble, and you shall never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and you shall find rest, and never be disquieted with madnesse.
What is heauier then lead? and what is the name of it, but a foole?
Sand, and salt, and a masse of yron is easier to beare then a man without vnderstanding.
As timber girt and bound together in a building, cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by aduised counsel, shal feare at no time.
A heart setled upon a thought of vnderstanding, is as a faire plaistering on the wall of a gallerie.
Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a feareful heart in the imagination of a foole, can not stand against any feare.
He that pricks the eye, wil make teares to fall: and he that pricks the heart, makes it to shewe her knowledge.
Who so casts a stone at the birds, frays them away, and he that vpbraids his friend, breaks friendship.
Though you drewest a sword at your friend, yet despaire not, for there way be a returning (to favor.)

If you have opened your mouth against your friend, feare not, for there may be a reconciliation: except for vpbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound, for, for these things every friend will depart.

Be faithfull to your neighbor in his pouertie, that you may reioyce in his prosperitie: abide stedfast to him in the time of his trouble, that you may be heire with him in his heritage: for a meane estate is not always to be contemned, nor the rich that is foolish, to be had in admiration.
As the vapour and smoke of a furnace goes before the fire: so reuiling before blood.
I will not be ashamed to defend a friend: neither will I hide myself from him.
And if any evil happen to me by him, every one that hears it will beware of him.
Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seale of wisdom upon my lippes, that I fall not suddenly by them, & that my tongue destroy me not?

verses.t: O Lord, father and gouernour of all my whole life, leaue me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.
Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for my ignorances and it passe not by my sins:
Least my ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before my aduersaries, and my enemie reioyce over me, whose hope is farre from your mercy.
O Lord, father and God of my life, give me not a proud looke, but turne away from your seruants always a haughty minde:
Turne away from me vaine hopes, and concupiscence, and you shall hold him up that is desirous always to serue you.
Let not the greedinesse of the belly, nor lust of the flesh take hold of me, and give not over me your seruant into an impudent minde.
Heare, O you children, the discipline of the mouth: He that keeps it, shall never be taken in his lippes.
The sinner shall be left in his foolishnesse: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.
Accustome not your mouth to swearing: neither vse yourself to the naming of the holy one.
For as a seruant that is continually beaten, shall not be without a blew marke: so he that swears and names God continually, shal not be faultlesse.

A man that vses much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: If he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence, and if he sweare in vaine, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.
There is a word that is clothed about with death: God graunt that it be not found in the heritage of Iacob, for all such things shall be farre from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins.
Use not your mouth to vntemperate swearing, for in it is the word of sin.

Remember your father and your mother, when you sit among great men. Be not forgetfull before them, and so you by your custome become a foole, and wish that you had not beene borne, and curse the day of your natiuitie.
The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will never be reformed all the daies of his life.

Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot minde is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicatour in the body of his flesh, will never cease till he has kindled a fire.
All bread is sweete to a whoremonger, he will not leaue off till he die.

A man that breaks wedlocke, saying thus in his heart, Who sees me? I am compassed about with darknesse: the walles couer me; & no body sees me, what neede I to feare? The most high wil not remember my sins:
Such a man only fears the eies of men, and knows not that the eies of the Lord are tenne thousand times brighter then the Sun, beholding all the waies of men, and considering the most secret parts.
He knew all things ere ever they were created, so also after they were perfited, he looked upon them all:
This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspects not, he shall be taken.
Thus shall it go also with the wife, that leaus her husband, and brings in an heire by another:
For first she has disobeyed the Law of the most High: and secondly, she has trespassed against her own husband, and thirdly, she has played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.
She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children.
Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring foorth no fruit.
She shall leaue her memory to be cursed, and her reproch shall not be blotted out.
And they that remaine, shall know that there is nothing better then the feare of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter then to take heed to the Commandement of the Lord.
It is great glory to follow the Lord, & to be receiued of him is long life.

verses.t: Wisdom shall praise her self, and shall glory in the midst of her people.
In the Congregation of the most high, shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.
I came out of the mouth of the most High, and couered the earth as a cloud.
I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottome of the deepe.
In the waues of the sea, and in all the earth, and in every people, and nation, I got a possession.
With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?
So the creatour of all things gaue me a commandement, and he that made me, caused my tabernacle to rest: and said, Let your dwelling be in Iacob, and your inheritance in Israel.
He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never faile.
In the holy Tabernacle I serued before him: and so was I established in Sion.
Likewise in the beloued city he gaue me rest, and in Jerusalem was my power.
And I tooke roote in an honourable people, euen in the portion of the Lords inheritance.
I was exalted like a Cedar in Libanus, and as a Cypresse tree upon the mountaines of Hermon.
I was exalted like a palme tree in Engaddi, and as a rose-plant in Iericho, as a faire oliue tree in a pleasant fielde, and grew up as a planetree by the water.
I gaue a sweete smell like cinamon, and aspalathus, and I yeelded a pleasant odour like the best mirrhe, as Galbanum and Onix, and sweet Storax, and as the sume of franckincense in the Tabernacle.
As the Turpentine tree, I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honor and grace.
As the Uine brought I foorth pleasant sauour, and my flowers are the fruit of honor and riches.
I am the mother of faire love, and feare, and knowledge, and holy hope, I therefore being eternall, am given to all my children which are named of him.
Come to me all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
For my memorial is sweeter then hony, and my inheritance then the hony combe.
They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drinke me shall yet be thirstie.
He that obeys me, shall never be confounded, and they that work by me, shall not do amisse.
All these things are the book of the Couenant of the most high God, euen the Law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the Congregations of Iacob.
Faint not to be strong in the Lord; that he may confirme you, cleaue to him: for the Lord Almightie is God alone, and besides him there is no other Savior.
He fills all things with his wisdome, as Physon, and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
He makes the vnderstanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Iorden in the time of the haru.
He makes the doctrine of knowledge appeare as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.
The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.
For her thoughts are more then the Sea, and her counsels profounder then the great deepe.
I also came out as a brooke from a riuer, and as a conduit into a garden.
I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bedde: and loe, my brooke became a riuer, and my riuer became a sea.
I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afarre off.
I will yet powre out doctrine as prophecie, and leaue it to all ages for ever.
Look that I have not laboured for myself onely, but for all them that seeke wisdom.

verses.t: Blessed is the man that has a vertuous wife, for the number of his dayes shall be double.
A vertuous woman reioycs her husband, and he shall fulfill the years of his life in peace.
A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that feare the Lord.
Whether a man be rich or poore, if he have a good heart towards the Lord, he shall at all times reioyce with a cheerefull countenance.

There be three things that mine heart fears: and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an vnruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse then death.
But a griefe of heart and sorrow, is a woman that is ielous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicats withall.
An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that has hold of her, is as though he held a scorpion.
A drunken woman and a gadder abroad, causes great anger, and she will not couer her own shame.
The whordome of a woman may be knowen in her haughtie lookes, and eye lids.
If your daughter be shamelesse, keepe her in straitly: lest she abuse her self through ouermuch libertie.
Watch over an impudent eye: and marueile not, if she trespasse against you.
She will open her mouth as a thirstie traueiler, when he has found a fountaine: and drinke of every water near her: by every hedge will she sit downe, and open her quiuer against every arrow.
The grace of a wife delights her husband, and her discretion will fat his bones.
A silent and louing woman is a gift of the Lord, and there is nothing so much worth, as a mind well instructed.
A shamefast and faithfull woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.
As the Sun when it arises in the high heaven: so is the beautie of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
As the cleare light is upon the holy candlesticke: so is the beautie of the face in ripe age.
As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of siluer: so are the faire feete with a constant heart.
My son, keepe the flowre of your age sound: and give not your strength to strangers.
When you have gotten a fruitfull possession through all the field: sowe it with your own seede, trusting in the goodnesse of your stocke.
So your race which you leau shall be magnified, hauing the confidence of their good descent.
An harlot shall be accounted as spittle: but a maried woman is a towre against death to her husband.
A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that fears the Lord.
A dishon woman contemns shame, but an honest woman will reuerence her husband.
A shamelesse woman shall be counted as a dog: but she that is shamefast will feare the Lord.
A woman that honours her husband, shall be judged wise of all: but she that dishonours him in her pride, shall be counted vngodly of all.
A loude crying woman, and a scolde, shall be sought out to driue away the enemies.

There be two things that grieue my heart: and the third makes me angry: a man of warre that suffers pouerty, and men of vnderstanding that are not set by: and one that returns from righteousness to sin: the Lord prepars such a one for the sword.
A merchant shall hardly keepe himself from doing wrong: and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.

verses.t: Many have sinned for a smal matter: & he that seeks for abundance will turne his eies away.
As a naile sticks fast betweene the ioynings of the stones: so does sin sticke close betweene buying and selling.
Unlesse a man hold himself diligently in the feare of the Lord, his house shall soone be ouerthrowen.
As when one sifts with a sieue, the refuse remains, so the filth of man in his talke.
The furnace proous the potters vessell: so the triall of man is in his reasoning.
The fruite declars if the tree have beene dressed: so is the vtterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
Praise no man before you hear him speake, for this is the triall of men.
If you followest righteousness, you shall obtaine her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.
The birds will resort to their like, so will truth returne to them that practise in her.
As the Lyon lies in waite for the pray: so sin for them that work iniquity.
The discourse of a godly man is always with wisdom: but a foole changs as the Moone.
If you be among the vndiscreet, obserue the time: but be continually among men of vnderstanding.
The discourse of fooles is irksome, and their sport is in the wantonnesse of sin.
The talke of him that swears much, makes the haire stand vpright: and their braules make one stop his eares.
The strife of the proud is blood-shedding, and their reuilings are grieuous to the eare.
Who so discouers secrets, looses his credit: and shall never find friend to his minde.
Love your friend, and be faithfull to him: but if you bewray his secrets, follow no more after him.
For as a man has destroyed his enemie: so have you lost the love of your neighbor.
As one that lets a bird go out of his hand, so have you let your neighbor go; and shall not get him again.
Follow after him no more, for he is too far off, he is as a roe escaped out of the snare.
As for a wound it may be bound up, and after reuiling there may be reconcilement: but he that bewrays secrets is without hope.
He that winks with the eies works evil, and he that knows him will depart from him.
When you are present he will speake sweetly, and will admire your words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander your sayings.
I have hated many things, but nothing like him, for the Lord will hate him.
Who so casts a stone on high, casts it on his own head, and a deceitfull stroke shall make wounds.
Who so digs a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it.
He that works mischiefe, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know from where it comes.
Mockery and reproach are from the proud: but vengeance as a Lyon shall lie in waite for them.
They that reioyce at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare, and anguish shall consume them before they die.
Malice and wrath, euen these are abhominations, and the sinfull man shall have them both.

verses.t: He that reuengs shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keepe his sins (in remembrance.)
Forgiue your neighbor the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you pray.
One man bears hatred against another, and does he seeke pardon from the Lord?
He shews no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he aske forgiuenesse of his own sins?
If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?
Remember your end, and let enimitie cease, corruption and death, and abide in the Commandements.
Remember the Commaundements, & beare no malice to your neighbor: the Couenant of the highest, and winke at ignorance.
Abstaine from strife, and you shall diminish your sins: for a furious man will kindle strife.
A sinfull man disquiets friends, and makes debate among them that be at peace.

As the matter of the fire is, so it burns: and as a mans strength is, so is his wrath, and according to his riches his anger rises, and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed.
An hastie contention kindls a fire, and an hasty fighting sheds blood.
If you blow the sparke, it shall burne: if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched, and both these come out of your mouth.
Curse the whisperer, and double tongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.
A backbiting tongue has disquieted many, and driuen them from nation to nation, strong cities has it pulled down, and ouerthrowen the houses of great men.
A backbiting tongue has cast out vertuous women, and depriued them of their labours.
Who so hearkens to it, shall never find rest, and never dwel quietly.
The stroke of the whip makes markes in the flesh, but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.
Well is he that is defended from it, and has not passed through the venime of it: who has not drawen the yoke of it, nor has bene bound in her bands.
For the yoke of it is a yoke of yron, and the bands of it are bandes of brasse.
The death therof is an evil death, the graue were better then it.
It shall not have rule over them that feare God, neither shall they be burnt with the flame of it.
Such as forsake the Lord shall fall into it, and it shall burne in them, and not be quenched, it shall be sent upon them as a Lion, and deuoure them as a Leopard.
Looke that you hedge your possession about with thornes, and binde up your siluer and gold:
And weigh your words in a ballance, and make a doore and barre for your mouth.
Beware you slide not by it, lest you fall before him that lies in wait.
