verses.t: He that is mercifull, will lende to his neighbor, and he that strengthns his hande, keeps the Commandements.
Lend to your neighbor in time of his need, and pay your neighbor again in due season.
Keepe your word & deale faithfully with him, and you shall always find the thing that is necessary for you.
Many when a thing was lent them, reckoned it to be found, and put them to trouble that helped them.

Till he has receiued, he will kisse a mans hand: and for his neighbours money he will speake submissely: but when he should repay, he will prolong the time, and returne words of griefe, and complaine of the time.

If he preuaile, he shall hardly receiue the halfe, and he will count as if he had found it: if not; he has depriued him of his money, and he has gotten him an enemy without cause: he payes him with cursings, and raylings: and for honor he will pay him disgrace.
Many therefore have refused to lend for other mens ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded.
Yet have you patience with a man in poore estate, and delay not to show him mercy.
Helpe the poore for the commandements sake, and turne him not away because of his pouertie.
Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and let it not rust under a stone to be lost.
Lay up your treasure according to the commandements of the most high, and it shall bring you more profite then golde.
Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliuer you from all affliction.
It shal fight for you against your enemies, better then a mightie shield and strong speare.
An honest man is suretie for his neighbor: but he that is impudent, will forsake him.
Forget not the friendship of your suretie: for he has given his life for you.
A sinner will ouerthrow the good estate of his suretie:
And he that is of an vnthankfull minde, will leaue him in that deliuered him.
Suretiship has vndone many of good estate, and shaked them as a waue of the Sea: mightie men has it driuen from their houses, so that they wandred among strange nations.
A wicked man transgressing the commandements of the Lord, shall fall into suretiship: and he that vndertaks and follows other mens businesse for gaine, shall fall into suits.
Helpe your neighbor according to your power, and beware that yourself fall not into the same.
The chiefe thing for life is water and bread, and clothing, and an house to couer shame.
Better is the life of a poore man in a meane cottage, then delicate fare in another mans house.
Be it little or much, holde you contented, that you heare not the reproch of your house.
For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where you are a stranger, you dare not open your mouth.
You shall entertaine and feast, and have no thankes: moreouer, you shall heare bitter words.
Come stranger, and furnish a table, and feede me of that you have ready.
Give place you stranger to an honourable man, my brother comes to be lodged, and I have neede of mine house.
These things are grieuous to a man of vnderstanding: the vpbraiding of house-roome, and reproching of the lender.

verses.t: He that loves his son, causes him oft to feele the rodde, that he may have ioy of him in the end.
He that chastises his son, shall have ioy in him, and shall reioyce of him among his acquaintance.
He that teaches his son, grieus the enemie: and before his friends he shall reioyce of him.
Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he has left one behinde him that is like himself.
While he lived, he saw and reioyced in him: and when he died he was not sorrowfull.
He left behinde him an auenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindnesse to his friends.
He that makes too much of his son, shall binde up his wounds, and his bowels wil be troubled at every cry.
An horse not broken becoms headstrong: and a childe left to himself will be wilfull.
Cocker your childe, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he will bring you to heauinesse.
Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow with him, and lest you gnash your teeth in the end.
Give him no liberty in his youth, and winke not at his follies.
Bow downe his necke while he is young, and beate him on the sides while he is a childe, lest he waxe stubborne, and be disobedient to you, and so bring sorrow to your heart.
Chastise your son, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behauiour be an offence to you.
Better is the poore being sound and strong of constitution, then a rich man that is afflicted in his body.
Health and good state of body are aboue all gold, and a strong body aboue infinite wealth.
There is no riches aboue a sound body, and no ioy aboue the ioy of the heart.
Death is better then a bitter life, or continuall sickenesse.
Delicates powred upon a mouth shut up, are as messes of meat set upon a graue.
What good does the offering to an idole? for neither can it eat nor smell: so is he that is persecuted of the Lord.
He sees with his eyes and grons, as an Eunuch that embracs a virgine, and sighs.
Give not over your mind to heauinesse, and afflict not yourself in your own counsell.
The gladnesse of the heart is the life of man, and the ioyfulnes of a man prolongs his dayes.
Love your own soul, and comfort your heart, remoue sorrow far from you: for sorrow has killed many, and there is no profit in it.
Enuie and wrath shorten the life, and carefulnesse brings age before the time.
A cherefull and good heart will have a care of his meat and diet.

verses.t: Watching for riches, consums the flesh, and the care therof drius away sleepe.
Watching care will not let a man slumber, as a sore disease breaks sleepe.
The rich has great labour in gathering riches together, and when he rests, he is filled with his delicates.
The poore labours in his poore estate, and when he leaus off, he is still needie.
He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that follows corruption, shall have enough of it.
Gold has been the ruine of many, and their destruction was present.
It is a stumbling block to them that sacrifice to it, and every foole shall be taken with it.
Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold:
Who is he? and we will call him blessed: for wonderfull things has he done among his people.
Who has bene tried thereby, and found perfit? then let him glory. Who might offend and has not offended, or done evil, and has not done it?
His goods shall be established, and the congregatiō shall declare his alms.
If you sit at a bountifull table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meate on it.

Stretch not your hand whithersoeuer it looks, and thrust it not with him into the dish.

Eat as it becoms a man those things which are set before you: and deuoure not, lest you be hated.

When you sit among many, reach not your hand out first of all.

He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that follows corruption, shall have enough of it.

verses.t: If you be made the master (of the feast) lift not yourself up, but be among them as one of the rest, take diligent care for them, and so sit downe.
And when you have done all your office, take your place that you may be merry with them, and receiue a crowne for your well ordering of the feast.
Speake you that art the elder, for it becoms you, but with sound judgment, and hinder not musicke.
Powre not out words where there is a musitian, and show not forth wisdom out of time.
A consort of musicke in a banket of wine, is as a signet of Carbuncle set in gold.
As a signet of an Emeraud set in a work of gold, so is the melodie of musicke with pleasant wine.
Speake yong man, if there be need of you: and yet scarsely when you are twise asked:
Let your speach be short, comprehending much in few words, be as one that knows, and yet holds his tongue.
If you be among great men, make not yourself equall with them, and when ancient men are in place, vse not many words.
Before the thunder goes lightening: and before a shamefast man shall go favor.
Rise up betimes, and be not the last: but get you home without delay.
There take your pastime, & do what you will: but sin not by proud speach
And for these things blesse him that made you, and has replenished you with his good things.
Who so fears the Lord, will receiue his discipline, and they that seeke him early, shall find favor.
He that seeks the law, shall be filled with it: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat.
They that feare the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
A sinfull man will not be reproued, but finds an excuse according to his will.
A man of counsell will be considerate, but a strange and proud man is not daunted with feare, euen when of himself he has done without counsell.
Do nothing without aduice, and when you have once done, repent not.
Go not in a way wherein you may fall, and stumble not among the stones.
Be not confident in a plaine way.
And beware of your own children.
In every good work trust your own soul: for this is the keeping of the commandements.
He that beleeus in the Lord, takes heed to the commandement, and he that trusted in him, shall fare never the worse.

verses.t: There shall no evil happen to him that fears the Lord, but in temptation euen again he will deliuer him.
A wise man hates not the Law, but he that is an hypocrite in it, is as a ship in a storme.
A man of vnderstanding trusts in the Law, and the Law is faithfull to him, as an oracle.
Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard, and binde up instruction, and then make answere.
The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheele: and his thoughts are like a rolling axeltree.
A stallion horse is as a mocking friend, he neighs under every one that sits upon him.
Why does one day excell another? when as all the light of every day in the year is of the Sun.
By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
Some of them has he made high dayes, and hallowed them, and some of them has he made ordinary dayes.
And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.
In much knowledge the Lord has diuided them, and made their wayes diuers.
Some of them has he blessed, and exalted, and some of them has he sanctified, and set near himself: but some of them has he cursed, and brought low, and turned out of their places.
As the clay is in the potters hand to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as likes him best.
Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
So looke upon all the works of the most High, and there are two and two, one against another.
I awaked up last of all, as one that gathers after the grape-gatherers: by the blessing of the Lord I profited, and filled my wine-presse, like a gatherer of grapes.
Consider that I laboured not for myself onely, but for all them that seeke learning;
Heare me, O you great men of the people, and hearken with your eares you rulers of the Congregation:
Give not your son, and wife, your brother and friend power over you while you liu, and give not your goods to another, lest it repent you: and you intreat for the same again.
As long as you liu and have breath in you, give not yourself over to any.
For better it is that your children should seeke to you, then that you shouldst stand to their courtesie.
In all your works keepe to yourself the preheminence, leaue not a staine in your honor.
At the time when you shall end your dayes, and finish your life, distribute your inheritance.
Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the asse: and bread, correction, and work for a seruant.
If you set your seruant to labour, you shall find rest: but if you let him go idle, he shall seeke libertie.
A yoke and a collar do bow the necke: so are tortures and torments for an evil seruant.
Sende him to labour that he be not idle: for idlenesse teaches much evil.
Set him to work, as is fit for him; if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.
But be not excessiue toward any, and without discretion do nothing.
If you have a seruant, let him be to you as yourself, because you have bought him with a price.
If you have a seruant, intreate him as a brother: for you have neede of him, as of your own soul: if you intreate him evil, and he runne from you, which way will you go to seeke him?

verses.t: The hopes of a man voyd of vnderstanding are vaine, and false: and dreames lift up fooles.
Who so regards dreames, is like him that catches at a shadow, and follows after the winde.
The vision of dreames is the resemblance of one thing to another, euen as the likenesse of a face to a face.
Of an unclean thing, what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false, what truth can come?
Diuinations, and soothsayings, and dreames are vaine: and the heart fancies as a womans heart in trauell.
If they be not sent from the most high in your visitation, set not your heart upon them.
For dreames have deceiued many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
The Law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithfull mouth.
A man that has trauailed knows many things: and he that has much experience, wil declare wisdom.
He that has no experience, knows little: but he that has trauailed, is full of prudence.
When I trauailed, I saw many things: and I vnderstand more, then I can expresse.
I was oft times in danger of death, yet I was deliuered because of these things.
The spirit of those that feare the Lord shall live, for their hope is in him that saus them.
Who so fears the Lord, shall not feare nor be afraid, for he is his hope.
Blessed is the soul of him that fears the Lord: to whom does he looke? and who is his strength?

For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mightie protection, and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a couer from the Sun at noone, a preseruation from stumbling, and a helpe from falling.
He raises up the soul, and lightens the eyes: he gives health, life, and blessing.
He that sacrifics of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous, and the giftes of vniust men are not accepted.
The most high is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked, neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
Who so brings an offering of the goods of the poore, does as one that kills the son before his fathers eyes.
The bread of the needie, is their life: he that defrauds him of it, is a man of blood.
He that takes away his neighbours living, slays him: and he that defrauds the labourer of his hire, is a bloodshedder.
When one builds, and another puls downe, what profite have they then but labour?
When one prays, and another curses, whose voice will the Lorde heare?
He that washes himself after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what auails his washing?
So is it with a man that fasts for his sins, and goes again and does the same: who will heare his prayer, or what does his humbling profit him?

verses.t: He that keeps the law, brings offerings enow: he that takes heed to the commandement, offers a peace offering.
He that requits a good turne, offers fine floure: and he that gives alms, sacrifics praise.
To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord: and to forsake vnrighteousnesse, is a propitiation.
You shall not appeare emptie before the Lord:
For all these things because of the commandement.
The offering of the righteous makes the Altar fat, and the sweete sauour of it is before the most high.
The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable, and the memoriall of it shall never be forgotten.
Give the Lord his honor with a good eye, and diminish not the first fruits of your hands.
In all your gifts show a cheerefull countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladnesse.
Give to the most high, according as he has enriched you, and as you have gotten, give with a cheerefull eye.
For the Lord recompenses, and will give you seuen times as much.
Do not think to corrupt with gifts, for such he will not receiue: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices, for the Lord is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.
He will not accept any person against a poore man: but will heare the prayer of the oppressed.
He will not despise the supplication of the fatherlesse: nor the widowe when she powrs out her complaint.
Does not the teares run downe the widowes cheeks? and is not her crie against him that causes them to fall?
He that serus the Lord, shall be accepted with favor, and his prayer shall reach to the cloudes.
The prayer of the humble piercs the clouds: and till it come near he will not be comforted: and will not depart till the most High shall beholde to judge righteously, and execute judgment.

For the Lord wil not be slacke, neither will the mightie be patient towards them, till he has smitten in sunder the loines of the vnmercifull, and repaid vengeance to the heathen: till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the scepter of the unrighteous:
Till he have rendred to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their deuises, till he have judged the cause of his people: and made them to reioyce in his mercy,
Mercie is seasonable in the time of affliction, as cloudes of raine in the time of drought.

verses.t: Have mercy upon us, O Lord God of all, and look us:
And send your feare upon all the nations that seeke not after you.
Lift up your hand against the strange nations, and let them see your power.
As you were sanctified in us before them: so be you magnified among them before us.
And let them know you, as we have knowen you, that there is no God, but onely you, O God.
Show new signes, and make other strange wonders: glorifie your hand and your right arme, that they may set forth your wonderous works.
Raise up indignation, and powre out wrath: take away the aduersarie and destroy the enemie.
Make the time short, remember the couenant, and let them declare your wonderfull works.
Let him that escaps, be consumed by the rage of the fire, and let them perish that oppresse the people.
Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.
Gather all the tribes of Iacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.
O Lord have mercy upon the people, that is called by your name, and upon Israel, whom you have named your first borne.
O be mercifull to Jerusalem your holy city, the place of your rest.
Fill Sion with your vnspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory.
Give testimonie to those that you have possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in your name.
Reward them that wait for you, and let your prophets be found faithfull.
O Lord heare the prayer of your seruants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all they which dwel upon the earth, may know that you are the Lord, the eternall God.
The belly deuours all meates, yet is one meat better then another.
As the palate tasts diuers kinds of venison: so does an heart of vnderstanding false speeches.
A froward heart causes heauinesse: but a man of experience will recompense him.
A woman will receiue every man, yet is one daughter better then another
The beautie of a woman chears the countenance, and a man loves nothing better.
If there be kindnesse, meekenes, and comfort in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.
He that gets a wife, begins a possession, a helpe like to himself, and a pillar of rest.
Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled: and he that has no wife will wander up and downe mourning.
Who will trust a thiefe well appointed, that skips from city to city? so a man that has no house? and lodgs wheresoeuer the night takes him?

The belly deuours all meates, yet is one meat better then another. As the palate tasts diuers kinds of venison: so does an heart of vnderstanding false speeches. A froward heart causes heauinesse: but a man of experience will recompense him. A woman will receiue every man, yet is one daughter better then another

The beautie of a woman chears the countenance, and a man loves nothing better. If there be kindnesse, meekenes, and comfort in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men. He that gets a wife, begins a possession, a helpe like to himself, and a pillar of rest. Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled: and he that has no wife will wander up and downe mourning. Who will trust a thiefe well appointed, that skips from city to city? so a man that has no house? and lodgs wheresoeuer the night takes him?

verses.t: Every friend saies, I am his friend also: but there is a friend which is onely a friend in name.
Is it not a griefe to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemie?
O wicked imagination, from where came you in to couer the earth with deceit?
There is a companion, which reioycs in the prosperity of a friend: but in the time of trouble will be against him.
There is a companion which helps his friend for the belly, and takes up the buckler against the enemie.
Forget not your friend in your minde, and be not vnmindfull of him in your riches.
Every counseller extols counsell; but there is some that counsels for himself.
Beware of a counseller, and know before what neede he has (for he will counsell for himself) lest he cast the lot upon you:
And say to you, Your way is good: and afterward he stand on the other side, to see what shall befall you.
Consult not with one that suspects you: and hide your counsell from such as enuie you.

Neither consult with a woman touching her of whom she is iealous; neither with a coward in matters of warre, nor with a merchant concerning exchange; nor with a buyer of selling; nor with an enuious man of thankfulnesse; nor with an vnmercifull man touching kindnesse; nor with the slouthfull for any work; nor with an hireling for a year, of finishing work; nor with an idle seruant of much businesse: Hearken not to these in any matter of counsell.
But be continually with a godly man, whom you know to keepe the commandements of the Lord, whose minde is according to your minde, and will sorrow with you, if you shall miscarry.
And let the counsell of your own heart stand: for there is no man more faithfull to you then it.
For a mans minde is sometime accustomed to tell him more then seuen watchmen, that sit aboue in an high towre.
And aboue all this pray to the most high, that he will direct your way in truth.
Let reason go before every enterprise, & counsell before every action.
The countenance is a signe of changing of the heart.
Foure maner of things appeare: good and evil, life and death: but the tongue rules over them continually.
There is one that is wise and teaches many, and yet is vnprofitable to himself.
There is one that shews wisdom in words, and is hated: he shall be destitute of all foode.
For grace is not given him from the Lord: because he is depriued of all wisdom.
Another is wise to himself: and the fruits of vnderstanding are commendable in his mouth.
A wise man instructs his people, and the fruits of his vnderstanding faile not.
A wise man shall be filled with blessing, and all they that see him, shall count him happy.
The daies of the life of man may be numbred: but the daies of Israel are innumerable.
A wise man shall inherite glory among his people, and his name shall be perpetuall.
My son prooue your soul in your life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that to it.
For all things are not profitable for all men, neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
Be not vnsatiable in any dainty thing: nor too greedy upon meates.
For excesse of meates, brings sicknesse, and surfetting will turne into choler.
By surfetting have many perished, but he that takes heed, prolongs his life.

verses.t: Honor a Phisitian with the honor due to him, for the vses which you may have of him: for the Lord has created him.
For of the most High comes healing, and he shall receiue honor of the King.
The skill of the Phisitian shall lift up his head: and in the sight of great men he shall be in admiration.
The Lord has created medicines out of the earth; and he that is wise will not abhorre them.
Was not the water made sweet with wood, that the virtue of it might be knowen?
And he has given men skill, that he might be honoured in his marueilous works.
With such does he heale and takes away their paines.
Of such does the Apothecarie make a confection; and of his works there is no end, and from him is peace over all the earth.
My son, in your sickenesse be not negligent: but pray to the Lord, and he will make you whole.
Leaue off from sin, and order your hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all wickedness.
Give a sweet sauour, and a memoriall of fine flowre: and make a fat offering, as not being.
Then give place to the phisitian, for the Lord has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.
There is a time when in their hands there is good successe.
For they shall also pray to the Lord, that he would prosper that, which they give, for ease and remedy to prolong life.
He that sins before his maker, let him fal into the hand of the Phisitian.
My son, let teares fall downe over the dead, and begin to lament, as if you had suffered great harme yourself: and then couer his body according to the custome, & neglect not his buriall.
Weepe bitterly, and make great moane, and vse lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: and then comfort yourself for your heauinesse.
For of heauinesse comes death, and the heauinesse of the heart, breaks strength.
In affliction also sorrow remains: and the life of the poore, is the curse of the heart.
Take no heauines to heart: driue it away, and remember the last end.
Forget it not, for there is no turning again: you shall not do him good, but hurt yourself.
Remember my judgment: for your also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for you.
When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest, & be comforted for him, when his spirit is departed from him.
The wisdom of a learned man cōmeth by opportunitie of leasure: & he that has litle busines shal become wise.
How can he get wisdome that holds the plough, and that glories in the goad; that drius oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talke is of bullocks?
He gives his minde to make furrowes: and is diligent to give the cattle fodder.

So every carpenter, and workemaster, that labours night and day: and they that cut and graue seales, and are diligent to make great variety, and give themselues to counterfait imagerie, and watch to finish a work.

The smith also sitting by the anuill, & considering the iron work; the vapour of the fire wasts his flesh, and he fights with the heat of the furnace: the noise of the hammer & the anuill is ever in his eares, and his eies looke still upon the patterne of the thing that he makes, he sets his mind to finish his work, & watches to polish it perfitly.
So does the potter sitting at his work, and turning the wheele about with his feet, who is always carefully set at his work: and makes all his work by number.
He fashions the clay with his arme, and bowes downe his strength before his feet: he applies himself to lead it over; and he is diligent to make clean the furnace.
All these trust to their hands: and every one is wise in his work.
Without these cannot a city be inhabited: and they shall not dwell where they will, nor go up and downe.

They shall not be sought for in publike counsaile; nor sit high in the congregation: they shal not sit on the Judges seate, nor vnderstand the sentence of judgment: they cannot declare justice, and judgment, and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.
But they will maintaine the state of the world, and their desire is in the work of their craft.

He will seeke out the secrets of graue sentences, and be conuersant in darke parables.

Hearken to me, you holy children, and budde foorth as a rose growing by the brooke of the field:
And give you a sweete sauour as frankincense, and flourish as a lilly, send foorth a smell, and sing a song of praise, blesse the Lord in all his works.
Magnifie his Name, and shewe foorth his praise with the songs of your lips, and with harpes, and in praising him you shall say after this maner:

verses.t: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you to a man that lius at rest in his possessions, to the man that has nothing to vexe him, and that has prosperity in all things: indeed to him that is yet able to receiue meate?
O death, acceptable is your sentence to the needy, and to him whose strength fails, that is now in the last age, and is vexed with all things, and to him that despairs and has lost patience.
Feare not the sentence of death, remember them that have beene before you, and that come after, for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.
And why are you against the pleasure of the most High? there is no inquisition in the graue, whether you have lived ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
The children of sinners, are abhominable children: and they that are conuersant in the dwelling of the vngodly.
The inheritance of sinners children shal perish, and their posterity shal have a perpetuall reproch.
The children will complaine of an vngodly father, because they shall be reproched for his sake.
Woe be to you vngodly men which have forsaken the law of the most high God: for if you encrease, it shall be to your destruction.
And if you be borne, you shall be borne to a curse: and if you die, a curse shall be your portion.
All that are of the earth shall turne to earth again: so the vngodly shall go from a curse to destruction.
The mourning of men is about their bodies: but an ill name of sinners shall be blotted out.
Have regard to your name: for that shall continue with you aboue a thousand great treasures of gold.
A good life has but few daies: but a good name endures for ever.
My children, keepe discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seene, what profit is in them both?
A man that hides his foolishnesse is better then a man that hides his wisdom.
Therefore be shamefast according to my word: for it is not good to retaine all shamefastnesse, neither is it altogether approoued in every thing.
Be ashamed of whoredome before father and mother, and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man:
Of an offence before a judge and ruler, of iniquitie before a congregation and people, of vniust dealing before your partner and friend:
And of theft in regard of the place where you soiourn, and in regard of the truth of God and his couenant, and to leane with your elbow upon the meate, and of scorning to give and take:
And of silence before them that salute you, and to look upon an harlot:
And to turne away your face from your kinsman, or to take away a portion or a gift, or to gaze upon another mans wife,
Or to be ouerbusie with his maide, and come not near her bed, or of vpbraiding speaches before friends; and after you have given, vpbraide not:
Or of iterating and speaking again that which you have heard, and of reuealing of secrets.
So shall you be truely shamefast, and find favor before all men.

verses.t: Of these things be not you ashamed, and accept no person to sin thereby.
Of the Law of the most High, and his Couenant, and of judgment to iustifie the vngodly:
Of reckoning with your partners, and traueilers: or of the gift of the heritage of friends:
Of exactnesse of ballance, and waights: or of getting much or little:
And of merchants indifferent selling, of much correction of children, and to make the side of an evil seruant to bleed.
Sure keeping is good where an evil wife is, and shut up where many hands are.
Deliuer all things in number and waight, and put al in writing that you give out, or receiu in.
Be not ashamed to informe the vnwise and foolish, and the extreeme aged that contends with those that are yong, thus shall you be truely learned and approued of all men living.
The father wakes for the daughter when no man knows, and the care for her takes away sleepe; when she is yong lest she passe away the flowre of her age, and being married, lest she should be hated:

In her virginitie lest she should be defiled, and gotten with childe in her fathers house; and hauing an husband, lest she should misbehaue herself: and when she is married, lest she should be barren.

Keepe a sure watch over a shamelesse daughter, lest she make you a laughing stocke to your enemies, and a by-word in the city, and a reproch among the people, and make you ashamed before the multitude.
Look not every bodies beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.
For from garments comes a moth, and from women wickedness.
Better is the churlishnesse of a man, then a courteous woman, a woman I say, which brings shame and reproch.
I will now remember the works of the Lord, and declare the things that I have seene: in the words of the Lord are his works.
The Sun that gives light, looks upon all things: and the work of it is full of the glory of the Lord.
The Lord has not given power to the Saints to declare all his marueilous works, which the Almightie Lord firmely setled, that whatsoeuer is, might be established for his glory.
He seeks out the deepe and the heart, and considers their crafty deuices: for the Lord knows all that may be knowen, and he beholds the signes of the world.
He declars the things that are past, and for to come, and reueils the steps of hidden things.
No thought escaps him, neither any word is hidden from him.
He has garnished the excellent works of his wisdom, and he is from euerlasting to euerlasting, to him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he has no need of any counseller.
O how desireable are all his works: and that a man may see euen to a sparke.
All these things live and remaine for ever, for all vses, and they are all obedient.
All things are double one against another: and he has made nothing vnperfit.
One thing establishes the good of another: and who shall be filled with beholding his glory?

verses.t: The pride of the height, the cleare firmament, the beautie of heaven, with his glorious show;
The Sun when it appears, declaring at his rising, a marueilous instrument, the work of the most High.
At noone it parches the country, and who can abide the burning heate of it?
A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the Sun burns the mountaines three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending foorth bright beames, it dims the eyes.
Great is the Lord that made it, and at his commandement it runs hastily.
He made the Moone also to serue in her season, for a declaration of times, and a signe of the world.
From the Moone is the signe of Feasts, a light that decreases in her perfection.
The month is called after her name, encreasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies aboue, shining in the firmament of heaven,
The beautie of heaven, the glory of the starres, an ornament giuing light in the highest places of the Lord.
At the commandement of the holy One, they will stand in their order, and never faint in their watches.
Looke upon the rainebow, and praise him that made it, very beautifull it is in the brightnesse of it.
It compass the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most high have bended it.
By his commandement he makes the snow to fall apace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his iudgment.
Through this the treasures are opened, and clouds flie forth as foules.
By his great power he makes the cloudes firme, and the hailestones are broken small.
At his sight the mountaines are shaken, and at his will the South wind blows.

The noise of the thunder makes the earth to tremble: so does the Northren storme, and the whirlewinde: as birds flying he scatters the snow, and the falling downe of it, is as the lighting of grashoppers.
The eye marueils at the beauty of the whitenesse of it, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it.
The hoare frost also as salt he powrs on the earth, and being congealed, it lies on the toppe of sharpe stakes.
Wheu the colde North-winde blows, and the water is congealed into yce, it abids upon every gathering together of water, and cloths the water as with a brestplate.
It deuours the mountaines, and burns the wildernesse, and consums the grasse as fire.
A present remedy of all is a miste comming speedily: a dew comming after heate, refreshes.
By his counsell he appeases the deepe, and plants Ilands in it.
They that saile on the Sea, tell of the danger of it, and when we heare it with our eares, we marueile thereat.
For in it be strange and wonderous works, varietie of all kindes of beasts, and whales created.
By him the ende of them has prosperous successe, and by his word all things consist.
We may speake much, & yet come short: therefore in summe, he is all.
How shall we be able to magnifie him? for he is great aboue all his works.
The Lord is terrible and very great, and marueilous is his power.
When you glorifie the Lord exalt him as much as you can: for euen yet wil he farre exceed, and when you exalt him, put foorth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can never go farre enough.
Who has seene him, that he might tell us? and who can magnifie him as he is?
There are yet hid greater things then these be, for we have seene but a few of his works:
For the Lord has made all things, and to the godly has he given wisdom.

verses.t: Let us now praise famous men, and our Fathers that begat us.
The Lorde has wrought great glory by them, through his great power from the beginning.
Such as did beare rule in their kingdomes, men renowmed for their power, giuing counsell by their vnderstanding, and declaring prophecies:
Leaders of the people by their counsels, and learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instructions.
Such as found out musical tunes, and reiected verses in writing.
Rich men furnished with abilitie, living peaceably in their habitations.
All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.
There be of them, that have left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported.
And some there be, which have no memorial, who are perished as though they had never bene, and are become as though they had never bene borne, and their children after them.
But these were mercifull men, whose righteousness has not beene forgotten.
With their seed shall continually remaine a good inheritance, and their children are within the couenant.
Their seed stands fast, and their children for their sakes.
Their seed shall remaine for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out.
Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lius for euermore.
The people will tell of their wisdome, and the congregation will show forth their praise.
Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance, to all generations.
Noah was found perfect and righteous, in the time of wrath, he was taken in exchange (for the world) therefore was he left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came.
An euerlasting Couenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.
Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like to him:
Who kept the Law of the most High, and was in couenant with him, he established the Couenant in his flesh, and when he was proued, he was found faithfull.

Therefore he assured him by an othe, that he would blesse the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him, as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the starres, and cause them to inherit from Sea to Sea, & from the riuer to the vtmost part of the land.
With Isaac did he establish likewise the blessing of all men and the couenant,
And made it rest upon the head of Iacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gaue him an heritage, and diuided his portions, among the twelue tribes did he part them.

verses.t: And he brought out of him a mercifull man, which found favor in the sight of all flesh, euen Moses beloued of God and men, whose memoriall is blessed:
He made him like to the glorious Saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in feare of him.
By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gaue him a commaundement for his people, and showed him part of his glory.
He sanctified him in his faithfulnesse, and meekenesse, and chose him out of all men.

He made him to heare his voice, and brought him into the darke cloud, and gaue him commandements before his face, euen the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Iacob his Couenants, and Israel his iudgments.
He exalted Aaron an holy man like to him, euen his brother, of the tribe of Leui.
An euerlasting couenant he made with him, and gaue him the priesthood among the people, he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.
He put upon him perfect glory: and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the Ephod:

And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bels round about, that as he went, there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the Temple, for a memoriall to the children of his people.
With an holy garment, with gold and blew silke, and purple the work of the embroiderer; with a brestplate of judgment, and with Urim & Thummim.

With twisted scarlet, the work of the cunning workeman, with precious stones grauen like seales, and set in gold, the work of the Ieweller, with a writing engraued for a memoriall, after the number of the tribes of Israel.
He set a crowne of gold upon the miter, wherein was engraued holinesse an ornament of honor, a costly work, the desires of the eies goodly & beautiful.
Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but onely his children, and his childrens children perpetually.
Their sacrifices shall be wholy consumed every day twise continually.

Moises consecrated him, and annointed him with holy oile, this was appointed to him by an euerlasting couenant, and to his seed so long as the heauens should remaine, that they should minister to him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and blesse the people in his name.
He chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense and a sweet sauour, for a memoriall, to make reconciliation for his people.
He gaue to him his commandements, and authority in the statutes of iudgements, that he should teach Iacob the testimonies, and informe Israel in his lawes.
Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wildernesse, euen the men that were of Dathans, and Abirons side, and the congregation of Core with fury and wrath.
This the Lord saw and it displeased him, and in his wrathfull indignation, were they consumed: he did wonders upon them, to consume them with the fiery flame.
But he made Aaron more honourable, and gaue him an heritage, and diuided to him the first fruits of the encrease, especially he prepared bread in abundance:
For they eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gaue to him and his seed:
However in the land of the people he had no inheritance, neither had he any portion among the people, for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance.

The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeale in the feare of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart, when the people were turned backe, and made reconciliation for Israel.

Therfore was there a couenant of peace made with him, that he should be the cheefe of the sanctuary, and of his people, and that he, and his posteritie should have the dignitie of the Priesthood for ever.

According to the couenant made with Dauid son of Iesse, of the tribe of Iuda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be to his seed.
God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.

According to the couenant made with Dauid son of Iesse, of the tribe of Iuda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be to his seed.
God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.

verses.t: Jesus the son of Naue was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophesies, who according to his name was made great for the sauing of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance.
How great glory got he when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities?
Who before him so stood to it? for the Lord himself brought his enemies to him.
Did not the Sun go backe by his meanes? and was not one day as long as two?
He called upon the most high Lord, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side, & the great Lord heard him.

And with hailestones of mighty power he made the battell to fall violently upon the nations, and in the descent (of Bethoron) he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength, because he fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the mightie one.
In the time of Moses also, he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Iephunne, in that they withstood the Congregation, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.
And of sixe hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserued to bring them into the heritage, euen to the land that flows with milk & hony.
The Lord gaue strength also to Caleb, which remained with him to his old age, so that he entred upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage.
That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
And concerning the Judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed.
Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honoured, be continued upon their children.
Samuel the Prophet of the Lord, beloued of his Lord, established a kingdom, & anointed princes over his people.
By the Law of the Lord he judged the Congregation, and the Lord had respect to Iacob.
By his faithfulnes he was found a true Prophet, and by his word he was knowen to be faithfull in vision.
He called upon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lambe.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.
And he destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, and all the princes of the Philistines.
And before his long sleepe he made protestations in the sight of the Lord, and his anoynted, I have not taken any mans goods, so much as a shoe, and no man did accuse him.
And after his death he prophesied, and showed the King his end, and lift up his voice from the earth in prophesie, to blot out the wickedness of the people.

verses.t: And after him rose up Nathan to prophesie in the time of Dauid.
As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was Dauid chosen out of the children of Israel.
He played with Lions as with kids, and with beares as with lambs.
Slew he not a gyant when he was yet but yong? and did he not take away reproch from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat downe the boasting of Goliah?
For he called upon the most high Lord, and he gaue him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warriour, and set up the horne of his people:
So the people honoured him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in that he gaue him a crowne of glory.
For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his aduersaries, and brake their horne in sunder to this day.
In all his works he praised the holy one most High, with words of glory, with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.
He set singers also before the Altar, that by their voyces they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs.
He beautified their feasts, and set in order the solemne times, until the ende, that they might praise his holy Name, and that the Temple might sound from morning.
The Lord tooke away his sins, and exalted his horne for ever: he gaue him a couenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.
After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large.
Salomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his Name, and prepare his Sanctuary for ever.
How wise were you in your youth, & as a flood filled with vnderstanding.
Your soul couered the whole earth, and you filledst it with dark parables.
Your name went farre to the Ilands, and for your peace you were beloued.
The countreys marueiled at you for your Songs, and Prouerbs, and Parables, and interpretations.
By the Name of the Lord God, which is called the Lord God of Israel, you did gather gold as tinne, and did multiply siluer as lead.
You did bow your loines to women, and by your body you were brought into subiection.
You dist staine your honor, and pollute your seed, so that you brought wrath upon your children, and were grieued for your folly.
So the kingdom was diuided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom.

But the Lord will never leaue off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: therefore he gaue a remnant to Iacob, and out of him a roote to Dauid.

Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seede he left behinde him Roboam, euen the foolishnesse of the people, and one that had no vnderstanding; who turned away the people through his counsell: there was also Ieroboam the son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin, and showed Ephraim the way of sin:
And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, that they were driuen out of the land.
For they sought out all wickednes, till the vengeance came upon them.

verses.t: Then stood up Elias the Prophet as fire, and his word burnt like a lampe.
He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeale he diminished their number.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought downe fire.
O Elias, how were you honoured in your wondrous deeds! and who may glory like to you!
Who did raise up a dead man from death, & his soul from the place of the dead by the word of the most Hie.
Who brought kings to destruction, and honourable men from their bedde.
Who heard the rebuke of the Lord in Sinai, and in Horeb the iudgment of vengeance.
Who anointed kings to take reuenge, & Prophets to succeed after him:
Who were taken up in a whirlewinde of fire, and in a charet of fierie horses:

Who were ordained for reproofes in their times, to pacifie the wrath of the Lordes judgment before it brake foorth into fury, and to turne the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Iacob.
Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love, for we shal surely live.
Elias it was, who was couered with a whirlewinde: and Elizeus was filled with his spirit: whil he lived he was not mooued of any prince, neither could any bring him into subiection.
No word could ouercome him, & after his death his body prophecied.
He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marueilous.

For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and caried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of Dauid:
Of whom, some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.
Ezekias fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst of it: he dug the hard rocke with yron, and made welles for waters.
In his time Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabsaces, and lift up his hand against Sion, & boasted proudly.
Then trembled their hearts and handes, and they were in paine as women in trauell.
But they called upon the Lord which is mercifull, and stretched out their hands towards him, and immediatly the holy One heard them out of heaven, and deliuered them by the ministery of Esay.
He smote the hoste of the Assyrians, and his Angel destroyed them.
For Ezekias had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the wayes of Dauid his father, as Esay the Prophet, who was great and faithfull in his vision, had commaunded him.
In his time the Sun went backeward, and he lengthened the kings life.
He sawe by an excellent spirit what should come to passe at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Sion.
He showed what should come to passe for ever, and secret things or ever they came.

verses.t: The remembrance of Iosias is like the composition of the perfume þ is made by the arte of the Apothecarie: it is sweete as hony in all mouthes, and as musicke at a banquet of wine.
He behaued himself vprightly in the conuersion of the people, and tooke away the abominations of iniquitie.
He directed his heart to the Lord, and in the time of the vngodly he established the worship of God.
All, except Dauid and Ezechias, and Iosias, were defectiue: for they forsooke the Law of the most High, (euen) the kings of Judah failed:
Therefore he gaue their power to others, & their glory to a strange nation.
They burnt the chosen city of the Sanctuarie, and made the streets desolate according to the prophecie of Ieremias:
For they entreated him evil, who neuerthelesse was a prophet sanctified in his mothers wombe, that he might root out and afflict & destroy, and that he might build up also and plant.
It was Ezechiel who sawe the glorious vision, which was showed him upon the chariot of the Cherubims
For he made mention of the enemies under the raine, and directed them that went right.
And of the twelue prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Iacob, and deliuered them by assured hope.
How shall we magnifie Zorobabel? euen he was as a signet on the right hand.
So was Jesus the son of Iosedec: who in their time built the house, and set up an holy Temple to the Lord, which was prepared for euerlasting glory.
And among the elect was Neemias whose renowme is great, who raised up for us, the walles that were fallen, and set up the gates & the barres, and raised up our ruines again.
But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch, for he was taken from the earth.
Neither was there a man borne like to Joseph, a gouernour of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.
Sem and Seth were in great honor among men, and so was Adam aboue every living thing in the creation.

verses.t: Simon the high priest the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his dayes fortified the Temple:
And by him was built from the foundation the double height, the high fortresse of the wall about the Temple.
In his dayes the cisterne to receiue water being in compasse as the sea, was couered with plates of brasse.
He tooke care of the Temple that it should not fall, and fortified the city against besieging.
How was he honoured in the midst of the people, in his comming out of the Sanctuarie?
He was as the morning starre in the midst of a cloud: and as the moone at the full.
As the Sun shining upon the Temple of the most High, and as the rainebow giuing light in the bright cloudes.
And as the flowre of roses in the spring of the year, as lillies by the riuers of waters, and as the branches of the frankincense tree in the time of summer.
As fire and incense in the censer, and as a vessell of beaten gold set with all maner of precious stones,
And as a faire oliue tree budding forth fruit, and as a Cypresse tree which grows up to the cloudes.
When he put on the robe of honor, and was clothed with the perfection of glory, when he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holinesse honourable.

When he tooke the portions out of the priests hands, he himself stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed with his brethren round about, as a yong cedar in Libanus, and as palme trees compassed they him round about.
So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of the Lord in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel.
And finishing the seruice at the altar, that he might adorne the offring of the most high Almighty,
He stretched out his hand to the cup, and powred of the blood of the grape, he powred out at the foote of the altar, a sweet smelling sauour to the most high King of all.
Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the siluer trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the most High.
Then all the people together hasted, and fell downe to the earth upon their faces to worship their Lord God almighty the most High.
The singers also sang praises with their voices, with great variety of sounds was there made sweete melodie.
And the people besought the Lord the most High by prayer before him that is mercifull, till the solemnity of the Lord was ended, and they had finished his seruice.
Then he went downe, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give the blessing of the Lord with his lips, and to reioyce in his name.
And they bowed themselues downe to worship the second time, that they might receiue a blessing from the most High.
Now therefore blesse you the God of all, which onely does wonderous things every where, which exalts our daies from the wombe, and deals with us according to his mercy.
He grant us ioyfulnesse of heart, and that peace may be in our daies in Israel for ever.
That he would confirme his mercy with us, and deliuer us at his time.
There be two maner of nations which my heart abhors, and the third is no nation.
They that sit upon the mountaine of Samaria, and they that dwell among the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.
Jesus the son of Sirach of Hierusalem has written in this book, the instruction of vnderstanding and knowledge, who out of his heart powred forth wisdom.
Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things, and he that layes them up in his heart, shall become wise.
For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things, for the light of the Lord leads him, who gives wisdom to the godly: blessed be the Lord for ever. Amen. Amen.

verses.t: I will thanke you, O Lord and king, and praise you O God my Savior, I do give praise to your name:

For you are my defeuder, and helper, and have preserued my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lippes that forge lies, and have beene my helper against my aduersaries.

And have deliuered me according to the multitude of your mercies, and greatnesse of your name, from the teeth of them that were ready to deuoure me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had:
From the choking of fire on every side, and from the mids of the fire, which I kindled not:
From the depth of the belly of hel, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words.
By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue, my soul drew near euen to death, my life was near to the hell beneath:
They compassed me on every side, and there was no man to helpe me: I looked for the succour of men, but there was none:
Then thought I upon your mercy, O Lord, and upon your acts of old, how you deliuer such as waite for you, and sau them out of the hands of the enemies:
Then lifted I up my supplication from the earth, and prayed for deliuerance from death.
I called upon the Lord the father of my Lord, that he would not leaue me in the dayes of my trouble, & in the time of the proud when there was no helpe.
I will praise your Name continually, and will sing praise with thanksgiving, and so my prayer was heard:
For you sauedst me from destruction, and deliuer me from the evil time: therefore will I give thankes and praise you, and blesse your Name, O Lord.
When I was yet yong, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer.

And have deliuered me according to the multitude of your mercies, and greatnesse of your name, from the teeth of them that were ready to deuoure me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had:

From the choking of fire on every side, and from the mids of the fire, which I kindled not: From the depth of the belly of hel, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words. By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue, my soul drew near euen to death, my life was near to the hell beneath: They compassed me on every side, and there was no man to helpe me: I looked for the succour of men, but there was none:
Then thought I upon your mercy, O Lord, and upon your acts of old, how you deliuer such as waite for you, and sau them out of the hands of the enemies:

Then lifted I up my supplication from the earth, and prayed for deliuerance from death.
